problem: Large Language Models (LLMs) often hallucinate on domain-specific tasks requiring reasoning; previous SG-RAG method improved over traditional RAG but still had redundancy in retrieved triplets.
method: Enhance SG-RAG with an additional Merging and Ordering Triplets (MOT) step: apply hierarchical merging on retrieved subgraphs to decrease redundancy and order triplets using BFS traversal to help LLMs generate more precise answers.
key_assumptions: Merging overlapping subgraphs reduces redundancy without losing essential information.
Ordering triplets via BFS helps LLMs utilize retrieved knowledge more effectively.
main_contribution: SG-RAG MOT provides more accurate answers than Chain-of-Thought and Graph Chain-of-Thought on the MetaQA benchmark by reducing redundancy and ordering retrieved triplets.
datasets: MetaQA benchmark (multi-hop question answering on movies domain)
metrics: Not stated explicitly; likely accuracy or hit@1
results: ["SG-RAG MOT provides more accurate answers than Chain-of-Thought and Graph Chain-of-Thought; merging and ordering triplets helps LLM generate more precise answers."]

relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: This work focuses on post-retrieval processing (merging and ordering) of subgraphs retrieved via SG-RAG. Our idea enriches training triples with local context subgraphs from the same passage and adds an adaptive repair loop for one-hop failures, targeting training data enrichment and iterative correction rather than retrieval post-processing.
